title: Infertility workup, semen analysis, tubal patency testing, ovarian reserve and assisted reproduction
subject: ss-obg
refs: WHO Laboratory Manual for the Examination and Processing of Human Semen (6th Edition 2021)
ASRM Practice Committee: Diagnostic evaluation of the infertile female

steps.say: Infertility is defined clinically as failure to achieve pregnancy after twelve months of regular unprotected sexual intercourse in women under 35 years. The etiological breakdown is balanced between partners, with male factor accounting for 30 percent, female tubal and ovulatory factors 50 percent, and unexplained infertility 15 to 20 percent.
steps.tx: The clinical definition of **infertility** requires failure to establish pregnancy after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse in women < 35 years (or 6 months in women >= 35 years). Etiologies divide into **male factor** (30 to 40 percent), **tubal factors** and ovulatory disorders (50 percent), and **unexplained infertility** (15 to 20 percent).

steps.say: Standardized evaluation of male fertility uses the World Health Organization sixth edition laboratory manual. Normal reference limits require a semen volume of at least 1.4 milliliters, sperm concentration of 16 million per milliliter, 42 percent total motility, and 4 percent normal morphological forms.
steps.tx: The **WHO 2021 semen analysis** reference standards establish lower reference limits: **semen volume** >= 1.4 mL, **sperm concentration** >= 16 million/mL (total count >= 39 million per ejaculate), progressive motility >= 30 percent (**total motility** >= 42 percent), and **normal morphology** >= 4.0 percent (strict Tygerberg criteria).

steps.say: Distinguishing between obstructive and non-obstructive azoospermia determines surgical sperm retrieval options. Obstructive azoospermia presents with normal testicular volume and normal FSH, whereas non-obstructive azoospermia manifests with small testes and elevated FSH, reflecting primary testicular failure.
steps.tx: Clinical evaluation of **azoospermia** differentiates into obstructive azoospermia (normal testicular volume, normal **serum FSH**, amenable to PESA/MESA) and **non-obstructive azoospermia** (small soft testes, markedly elevated FSH, requiring **microdissection TESE** to recover rare isolated foci of preserved testicular spermatogenesis for ICSI).

left.title: Obstructive Azoospermia
points: Sperm retrieval: PESA or MESA with > 95% yield

right.title: Non-Obstructive Azoospermia
points: Testicular volume: small, soft (< 10 to 12 mL)
Sperm retrieval: micro-TESE with 40 to 50% yield

steps.say: Serum anti-Mullerian hormone and antral follicle count serve as the most accurate quantitative biomarkers of ovarian reserve. Anti-Mullerian hormone produced by preantral granulosa cells remains constant across the menstrual cycle, where levels below 1.1 nanograms per milliliter predict diminished reserve.
steps.tx: Quantitative assessment of ovarian reserve employs **anti-Mullerian hormone** (AMH) and **antral follicle count** (AFC). Produced by preantral granulosa cells, AMH reflects the resting primordial pool; values under 1.1 ng/mL (or AFC < 5 to 7) indicate **diminished ovarian reserve**, while values > 3.5 ng/mL alert to hyper-response.

nodes.label: Measure serum AMH (independent of cycle day) and baseline day 2-3 AFC
AMH < 1.1 ng/mL or AFC < 5 to 7: diminished ovarian reserve (poor responder)
AMH 1.1 to 3.5 ng/mL or AFC 8 to 15: normal ovarian reserve (expected responder)
AMH > 3.5 ng/mL or AFC > 20: polycystic reserve (high risk for OHSS)

steps.say: Hysterosalpingography is the standard initial imaging test for assessing fallopian tube patency and intrauterine cavity contour. Fluoroscopic injection of water-soluble iodinated contrast during the early follicular phase confirms bilateral patency by demonstrating free peritoneal spill.
steps.tx: Initial evaluation of tubal architecture utilizes **hysterosalpingography** (HSG) performed on cycle day 7 to 10. Fluoroscopy using **water-soluble contrast** outlines the endometrial cavity and demonstrates **bilateral tubal patency** via free peritoneal spillage into the pouch of Douglas without vascular intravasation.

nodes.label: Schedule HSG in day 7 to 10 post-menstrual follicular window
Cannulate external cervical os and inject 5 to 10 mL water-soluble iodinated contrast
Document symmetrical triangular uterine fill and bilateral linear tubal transit
Confirm bilateral free contrast spillage outlining pelvic peritoneal contours

steps.say: Diagnostic laparoscopy with chromopertubation is the definitive gold standard for detecting subtle tubal pathology and pelvic endometriosis. Transcervical injection of dilute methylene blue or indigo carmine directly visualizes fimbrial spillage under general anesthesia.
steps.tx: **Diagnostic laparoscopy** combined with **chromopertubation** (using dilute methylene blue dye) represents the established gold standard for diagnosing tubal disease, peritubal fimbrial adhesions, and superficial **pelvic endometriosis** missed by hysterosalpingography, permitting concurrent surgical adhesiolysis and anatomical restoration of normal tubo-ovarian relationships.

left.title: Hysterosalpingography (HSG)
points: High sensitivity for proximal tubal occlusion and Asherman
Cannot evaluate extratubal pelvic adhesions or endometriosis

right.title: Laparoscopy & Chromopertubation
points: Gold standard surgical inspection under general anesthesia
Direct visualization of methylene blue spill from fimbrial ends
Permits concurrent surgical adhesiolysis and endometriosis ablation

steps.say: Intrauterine insemination washes and concentrates motile spermatozoa before direct placement into the uterine fundus at ovulation. The procedure requires at least one patent fallopian tube and a post-wash total motile sperm count exceeding five million.
steps.tx: **Intrauterine insemination** (IUI) is indicated for mild male factor, cervical hostility, or unexplained subfertility. It strictly mandates at least one documented **patent fallopian tube** and a post-wash **total motile sperm count** (TMSC) exceeding 5 to 10 million for acceptable fecundity.

rows: Patent fallopian tubes, post-wash TMSC > 5 million
Healthy viable oocytes, adequate motile sperm
Severe male factor, prior IVF failure
Single viable spermatozoon per mature MII oocyte

steps.say: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome is a life-threatening iatrogenic complication of controlled ovarian stimulation driven by vascular endothelial growth factor. Clinicians prevent severe OHSS by substituting a GnRH agonist trigger for hCG, followed by freeze-all embryo transfer.
steps.tx: **Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome** (OHSS) is a dangerous iatrogenic complication driven by granulosa cell **VEGF** secretion following gonadotropin stimulation. Severe cases feature third-space ascites and hemoconcentration, preventable by using a **GnRH agonist trigger** instead of hCG and adopting a **freeze-all embryo transfer** strategy.
